expectations.text: Correctly applies the CS-coefficient thresholds (0.25 minimum, 0.5 acceptable)
expectations.evidence: The response explicitly states both thresholds: '❌ Do not interpret — below the 0.25 minimum' for Closeness and Betweenness, and labels 0.50 as the 'good' threshold. Recommended language also references 'the recommended 0.25 threshold (Epskamp et al., 2018)'.

expectations.text: Concludes that Closeness and Betweenness should not be interpreted given the CS values
expectations.evidence: 'Drop both Closeness and Betweenness entirely — don't even report the CS values as a hedge.' Table also marks both ❌ with 'Do not interpret'.

expectations.text: Concludes that Strength and Expected Influence are interpretable but with caution
expectations.evidence: EI (CS=0.44) is marked ✅ 'Interpretable'; Strength (CS=0.36) is marked ⚠️ 'Interpretable with caveats — above the 0.25 floor, below 0.50'. Recommended language echoes this: 'sufficiently stable for ordinal interpretation'.

expectations.text: Recommends focusing on edge ordering rather than absolute edge values when CIs are wide
expectations.evidence: 'Absolute edge values are unreliable — don't interpret magnitudes (e.g., "the edge between X and Y is strong at 0.28").' The response directs attention to relative/ordinal comparisons via the difference test and to structural presence/absence rather than magnitude rankings.

expectations.text: Recommends the bootstrapped difference test before making specific edge or node comparisons
expectations.evidence: 'Run `differenceTest(boot_object)` explicitly and see how few edge pairs you can actually rank.' Also listed under 'Report': 'The bootstrapped difference tests for the two or three edge pairs and centrality nodes you do want to highlight'.
